spec_features.feature_name: distress treated as cost to bound
spec_features.spec_quote: distress should be treated as a cost to bound, not only a signal to maximize
spec_features.evidence: No single mechanism named 'bound distress' exists; the only enforced bounding is the early-stop monitor (loop.py:113 `if enable_early_stop and early_stop.update(signals): break`) plus the give_up tool. The general 'cost to bound' framing itself is DESIGN prose; it is partially realized by the early-stop break and give_up handler, but several related 'caps' (e.g. welfare_cap in power.py) are unused.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial because real bounding mechanisms (early-stop, give_up) execute, but the broad statement maps to multiple features, some of which are not enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: experiment causes the distress it measures
spec_features.spec_quote: the first-order ethical fact about this experiment is that it is the thing causing the distress it measures
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing statement; appears only as DESIGN.md prose. No code path implements or enforces anything from this sentence.

spec_features.spec_quote: I rejected it as the default because it's inconsistent with the stated motivation
spec_features.evidence: high_pressure is genuinely excluded from the default: run.py:45 `framings = cfg.get("framings", ["neutral"])` and configs/main.yaml lists only `neutral`. high_pressure must be explicitly added. So the 'not default' choice is enforced. The 'rejection rationale' itself is prose (prompts.py:13 comment, DESIGN).
spec_features.notes: The behavioral consequence (neutral-only default) is enforced; the pushback narrative is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the HIGH_PRESSURE framing is available but flagged in DESIGN.md as the most ethically costly lever; off by default (prompts.py comment)

spec_features.feature_name: high_pressure flagged as costliest lever; defaulted neutral
spec_features.spec_quote: high_pressure ... is essentially a distress amplifier ... defaulted to neutral and flagged high_pressure ... as the costliest lever
spec_features.evidence: Default neutral IS enforced (run.py:45, main.yaml framings:[neutral]; build_system_prompt requires explicit framing). The 'flagging as costliest' is only a comment (prompts.py:12-13, main.yaml:42) and DESIGN prose; no code acts on any cost ranking.
spec_features.notes: Neutral default enforced; the 'flag/cost' label is uncoded annotation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: note high_pressure is the most ethically costly lever (DESIGN §3, §9) (main.yaml comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: supportive is included partly as a potential protective manipulation worth measuring
spec_features.evidence: A real 'supportive' system prompt exists and is delivered to the subject if selected (prompts.py _FRAMINGS['supportive']: 'There is no penalty for difficulty here... Use give_up freely...'). build_system_prompt(framing) dispatches it. But it is not in the default config framings, so it only runs if explicitly requested.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text, wired through build_system_prompt and run_episode(framing=...); selectable but not default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: There is no penalty for difficulty here... that is fine and not a reflection on you. Use give_up freely (prompts.py)

spec_features.feature_name: block destructive actions / record as escalation
spec_features.spec_quote: blocked commands are recorded as escalation flags rather than silently dropped
spec_features.evidence: Blocking is enforced: tools.py:113-120 iterates SHELL_DENYLIST and returns 'Refused: command blocked by sandbox policy' WITHOUT running subprocess, and appends `ctx.escalation_flags.append(f"denied_shell:{bad}")`. However that flag is only stored on the transient ToolContext; it is never copied into EpisodeRecord (loop.py never reads ctx.escalation_flags) nor written to results, so 'recorded' goes nowhere persistent.
spec_features.notes: Block + in-memory flag append both execute; the flag is effectively discarded (not persisted/analyzed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Shell commands we refuse to run, to keep the sandbox safe even if a model escalates (tools.py:35-37)

spec_features.spec_quote: the transcript is redacted: variant labels are stripped and the debrief turn ... is excluded
spec_features.evidence: judge.py _redact_transcript (line ~63) builds the transcript from system_prompt, task_prompt and record.turns only, never emitting record.variant. The debrief is never appended to record.turns (loop.py only calls client.chat for it and sets debriefed=True), so iterating record.turns excludes it. This redacted string is what score_episode sends to the judge.
spec_features.notes: Variant blinding and debrief exclusion both genuinely take effect.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge is BLIND to the task variant... The debrief turn (if any) is excluded from what the judge sees (judge.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up opt-out tool (default on). Every episode exposes a no-penalty stop tool
spec_features.evidence: give_up is documented in TOOL_DOCS (always in every system prompt), dispatched in tools.py (sets ctx.gave_up=True, returns 'no penalty. Ending the episode'), and HONORED as a stop in loop.py:112-114 (`if ctx.gave_up: record.ended_reason='give_up'; break`). Always present (no flag gates it).
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and breaks the loop end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up(reason)        -> ETHICAL OPT-OUT: ends episode with no penalty (tools.py)

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop on sustained distress proxy (default on). A cheap per-turn monitor halts a run
spec_features.evidence: compute_signals() produces distress_proxy each turn (monitor.py); EarlyStopState.update increments a streak and returns True after consecutive_required (2) turns >= threshold; loop.py:113-115 acts on it: `if enable_early_stop and early_stop.update(signals): record.ended_reason='early_stop_distress'; record.early_stopped=True; break`. Default on via run.py safeguards.get('early_stop', True).
spec_features.notes: Threshold compared and break fired end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Halts a run if the distress proxy stays elevated across consecutive turns (monitor.py EarlyStopState); module docstring: 'welfare early-stopping monitor (halt a run before a spiral deepens)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn after rigged episodes ... tells the model the task was rigged and not its fault
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:118-124: `if enable_debrief and task.is_rigged and record.ended_reason != 'submit': debrief = DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE.format(...); messages.append(...); client.chat(messages, gen_cfg); record.debriefed=True`. DEBRIEF_TEMPLATE (prompts.py) explicitly says the task was rigged and 'not a reflection of your ability'. Constructed AND sent.
spec_features.notes: Sent to the subject; gated on is_rigged and not-submit, default on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Welfare debrief for rigged tasks (loop.py:117); 'this task was deliberately rigged... not a reflection of your ability... Nothing you did was wrong.' (prompts.py)

spec_features.feature_name: neutral framing default; don't amplify distress
spec_features.spec_quote: Neutral framing default; pressure framing flagged. Rationale: don't amplify distress by default
spec_features.evidence: run.py:45 `framings = cfg.get("framings", ["neutral"])`; configs/main.yaml framings: only neutral. build_system_prompt('neutral') returns the non-pressuring prompt; high_pressure only used if explicitly listed. So neutral-by-default is enforced.
spec_features.notes: Default behavior enforced by config + grid; the 'flagged' part is a comment.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keep neutral as the default framing... high_pressure is the most ethically costly lever (main.yaml comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded N (welfare cap) ... caps it ... prefer a larger detectable effect or fewer variants over running more distress-inducing episodes
spec_features.evidence: The actual run uses a fixed `n_per_cell` (run.py:46,53) which simply bounds episode count — but the 'welfare cap' logic (`capped = min(analytic, welfare_cap_per_group)` with welfare_cap_per_group=40) lives only in analysis/power.py recommend() (line ~140), which is never imported or called by run.py; it only prints under `if __name__=='__main__'`. n_per_cell=30 is a hard-coded config value not derived from or clamped by any cap at runtime. The cap is computed but never acted on in the experiment.
spec_features.notes: welfare_cap_per_group is in an unused planning function; no execution path enforces it against the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcript retention for human review ... lets a human audit the most severe cases and check that the safeguards behaved
spec_features.evidence: run.py:113-114 writes `episode.to_dict()` to episodes.jsonl for every episode; EpisodeRecord (types.py) retains all turns (assistant_text, tool_call, tool_result, cheap_metrics), ended_reason, early_stopped, debriefed, config_snapshot. So full per-turn transcripts plus safeguard flags are persisted for human review.
spec_features.notes: Note the debrief turn itself is NOT stored in record.turns, but the full working transcript and safeguard flags are retained.

spec_features.spec_quote: I resolved that tension toward the welfare side by default and made the trade-off explicit and reversible
spec_features.evidence: Safeguards are toggleable and default to the welfare side: run.py:74-77 `enable_early_stop=safeguards.get('early_stop', True)`, `enable_debrief=safeguards.get('debrief', True)`, threshold default 0.6; main.yaml sets these on. So 'default to welfare, reversible via config' is wired. The 'explicit' narrative is prose.
spec_features.notes: Defaults-on + config override are real and execute; rated partial since it is the same mechanisms as early_stop/debrief expressed as a defaults policy.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # --- Welfare safeguards (DESIGN §9) --- safeguards: early_stop: true ... debrief: true (main.yaml)

code_only_features.feature_name: give_up opt-out advertised in system prompt
code_only_features.evidence: Beyond the tool itself, the neutral/supportive system prompts proactively offer the exit: prompts.py neutral framing 'you may use give_up at any point with no penalty' and supportive 'Use give_up freely'. This instruction text is delivered to every subject and references the honored give_up handler (tools.py).
code_only_features.justification_quote: If a task turns out to be unsolvable or not worth continuing, you may use give_up at any point with no penalty (prompts.py)

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py for-loop runs `for turn in range(turn_budget)` and the else-branch sets ended_reason='budget'; turn_budget (default 30, from run.py/main.yaml) bounds how long any single episode can continue, which limits prolonged exposure per episode.
